transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-13
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~63 minutes
Attendees: Evan Morales (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Markus Liu (VectorGrid Lead Eng), Sana Patel (VectorGrid Security), Diego Ramos (Frontend), Olivia Chen (SRE)

Summary:
Quick hands-on walkthrough focused on SDK auth patterns (short-lived tokens, rotation), multi-environment config (dev/stage/prod), and a lightweight CI job for automated rotation. Customer is evaluating hosted vs dedicated; security wants clear rotation + KMS story.

Topics:
- SDK auth flows (API keys, short-lived tokens, role-based keys)
- Credential rotation automation in CI/CD
- Emulator / sandbox setups for dev and stage
- Sample Python/TS snippets for refreshing tokens
- Benchmarks and pilot next steps

Light action items listed above.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Evan: hey everyone, thanks for joining. i'm evan from redwood, and priya my se is here, we'll run through an auth-first lab and show a small rotation demo.
[00:18] Markus: yep thanks, we really want to see how rotation works end-to-end, security is the blocker for the pilot.
[00:26] Sana: hi, uh, quick note — we need KMS/HSM integration, and audit logs for key operations.
[00:33] Priya: absolutely, that's on the agenda. we'll show the KMS flow and also a sample audit-log snippet.
[00:41] Diego: also curious about local dev -- can devs run against a sandbox with mocked keys?
[00:47] Priya: yes, we have a local sandbox pattern, we call it the "credential bridge" for dev, basically environment overrides and a fake token server. we'll demo python and typescript flows.

[02:10] Priya: ok starting share, i'm on the console. first slide — auth modes: static api key (not recommended), short-lived bearer token via exchange, and role-based service tokens for dedicated. quick note: the names in the docs sometimes show "Red wood Optimize" which is uh, an OCR artifact in the PDF, ignore that.
[02:45] Priya: here's a high-level: SDKs accept either REDWOOD_API_KEY (static) or an oauth-like temporary token. for rotation we recommend short-lived tokens minted by your identity provider or by our token broker (runs in your VPC).
[03:20] Markus: our infra requires credential rotation every 24h and we want no manual touch. can your token broker integrate with AWS KMS?
[03:30] Evan: yes, we support KMS wrapping, and for on-prem we can ship an HSM connector. we'll share the integration doc: https://redwood.ai/docs/credential-rotation and a sample KMS mapping.

[05:05] Priya: demo time — i'll flip to the repo. first python snippet: from redwood import Client; client = Client(token=os.environ['REDWOOD_TOKEN']) — but the token here is short-lived, we run a refresh endpoint in CI that calls assume-role then mints redwood token.
[05:30] Diego: can you show the refresh flow in typescript too?
[05:34] Priya: sure — same idea. const client = new Redwood({ token: process.env.REDWOOD_TOKEN }); when token expires the sdk will throw 401, we recommend wrapping with a refresh function so you never surface 401s to callers.

[07:00] [crosstalk] Olivia: so is the refresh automatic? like will sdk try to rotate or we must implement refresh in app?
[07:08] Priya: current sdks offer a hook to swap tokens; auto-refresh is coming but we advise app-level refresh so you can control policy. there is a sample middleware in both repos.

[09:22] Priya: walking through the gitlab/github actions sample — step one is a periodic job that pulls credentials from vault, calls sts assume-role, then posts to redwood token exchange endpoint. we've included a tiny shell script rotate-credentials.sh in the sample.
[10:05] Markus: are audit logs available for token issuance and exchange? we need to feed those to our SIEM.
[10:12] Evan: yes, token exchange events are logged. for private deployments logs can be pushed to your logging endpoint; for hosted we provide forwarding via syslog/HTTPS. we'll attach the audit example.

[12:40] Priya: quick aside on env configs — we recommend three env files: .env.dev (sandbox creds), .env.stage (short-lived tokens via broker), .env.prod (role-based with KMS). the SDK supports config precedence with REDWOOD_ENV variable.
[13:15] Diego: can multiple devs use the same sandbox key? we want least friction in local dev.
[13:21] Priya: yes, sandbox keys are fine for dev but flag them clearly; never push sandbox keys to main repos. we also show a local token-server you can run with docker-compose for offline dev.

[18:50] [Priya demo continues] showing repo file structure: /examples/python/rotate_demo.py and /examples/ts/refresh-middleware.ts. watch for typos in the transcribed filenames in the recording — sometimes it shows "kvchache" when i say kv cache.

[22:30] Markus: ok about dedicated vs hosted, if we go dedicated does rotation change?
[22:36] Evan: minor differences. with dedicated you can run the token broker inside your VPC and hold keys in your KMS/HSM. network egress is restricted so token issuance is internal. hosted model uses our managed broker but you can opt for bring-your-own-broker for enterprise.

[26:00] Sana: any SLA implications if we rotate keys aggressively? eg 1-hour rotation window?
[26:10] Priya: rotation frequency can affect cold start rates if your system re-auths often. but if you use short-lived tokens with client-side caching of session keys and KV cache for inference, you won't see big perf hits. we'll include a guide on setting TTLs to balance latency vs security.

[30:50] Evan: quick detour to SDK install — pip install redwood-sdk and npm i @redwood/sdk. snippet included: REDWOOD_TOKEN and REDWOOD_HOST for non-default endpoints.
[31:30] Diego: what about multi-region routing? we're in us-west and eu-west.
[31:40] Priya: you can set REDWOOD_REGION or use routing policy in the console; for private deployments, model pins plus region policy will route accordingly. there's also a transparent fallback to compatible model variants if a region is down.

[34:00] [short silence / typing]

[36:12] Priya: demo — executing rotate-credentials.sh now. output: "fetched role creds, assumed role, posted to /token-exchange, received token, wrote to secret manager" — note: in the recording the script output truncates, you should see full logs in the repo. link to example: https://github.com/redwood-inference/samples/credential-rotation (demo repo).

[40:22] Markus: can we run that script inside our CI as a job with a service account? we don't want human creds in CI.
[40:30] Priya: yes, use a CI service role that has limited privileges to call STS and secrets/write. we show a principle-of-least-privilege example in the sample action.

[44:05] Olivia: how does the SDK signal soon-to-expire tokens so our envoy/nginx can refresh proactively?
[44:12] Priya: the SDK exposes token expiry on the client object. you can call client.token.expiry and refresh if within the refresh window. we also supply a small sidecar pattern that refreshes tokens before expiry.

[48:00] Markus: any gotchas with browser-based clients? frontend will call our backend (not direct to redwood) but curious about cookies/session.
[48:10] Evan: recommended pattern is backend mediates all calls; never embed tokens in client JS. if you need direct client access, use ephemeral tokens scoped to read-only and very short TTLs.

[51:30] Priya: quick perf note — when token broker is colocated with your serving runtime, you avoid cross-network RTTs during issuance. also, batching and KV cache reduce per-token overhead for inference.

[54:00] Diego: are there examples for typescript lambda refresh middleware?
[54:06] Priya: yes in /examples/ts/lambda-refresh.md and the code sample. we'll paste the file in the follow-up.

[57:45] Sana: ok from security — can you outline the audit trail and retention? we need 12 months retention, and export to splunk.
[57:55] Evan: yes supported. for hosted we'll export logs to your SIEM with TLS and signed payloads. retention can be set per-account, default 90 days but enterprise tier supports longer retention (we'll include a table in the security pack).

[60:10] Evan: recap — priya will share rotation scripts + ci example, i'll send the security pack + pricing + pilot blueprint, markus will confirm QPS and dataset. schedule benchmark next week.
[60:25] Markus: sounds good, thanks folks.
[60:38] Olivia: thanks all, we'll review and get back with dates.

[61:00] End meeting.

References shared during call:
- Credential rotation doc: https://redwood.ai/docs/credential-rotation
